oVtVZXdBzP4.description:
🥣 Leroy’s Homemade Granola
Prep Time: 10 minutesCook Time: 2 hoursOven Temp: 190°FYield: Large batch
Ingredients
Dry Ingredients
* 8 cups rolled oats
* 1 cup shredded coconut
* 1 cup sesame seeds
* 1 cup sunflower seeds
* 1 cup dried milk powder
* ½ teaspoon salt
Wet Ingredients
* 1 cup oil
* 1 cup honey
* 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
* 1 teaspoon cinnamon
Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 190°F.
2. Mix dry ingredientsIn a large bowl, combine oats, coconut, sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, dried milk powder, and salt.
3. Blend wet ingredientsIn a blender, blend the oil, honey, vanilla, and cinnamon until well combined.
4. CombinePour the blended wet mixture over the dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly until everything is evenly coated.
5. Prepare panSpray a large baking sheet or roasting pan with nonstick spray. Spread the granola mixture evenly across the pan.
6. BakeBake for 1 hour.
7. Mix and finish bakingRemove from oven, mix the granola well, spread it back out evenly, and bake for another 1 hour.
8. Cool
Let  the granola cool completely before storing.
Storage
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2–3 weeks.
Optional Add-Ins (after baking)
* Raisins
* Dried cranberries
* Chopped almonds or pecans
* Chocolate chips

cjIPFMfq8OQ.description:
December 29, 2006, at 6:43 in the evening, you slipped away with one last gentle breath. I knew the moment you were gone. That day changed everything. It was the most painful day your dad and I have ever known. And still, somehow, we found a quiet sense of peace in knowing your struggle was over and that pain no longer touched you.
I remember holding you, memorizing the feel of you in my arms, moving slowly through the room because I wasn't ready to say goodbye. Time seemed to stand still, as if letting go might make the loss real. Walking out of the hospital for the last time felt unreal, like leaving a piece of my heart behind. How could the world keep moving when you were no longer in it?
I'll never forget the small details. The room, the sounds, the view outside and the weather. Logan, you are forever a part of me.
Thank you for allowing me to be your mother. I can't wait to be reunited with you one day and raise you in a perfect world.

OcxnvIwZ0ec.description: Yesterday, my niece, Alyssa had her wisdom teeth extracted. With her kind consent, I’d like to share a video capturing this memorable moment. For those who may not know, Alyssa is staying with us while attending college and plays a vital role in Kesley Jade Collections, where she excels. We adore having her in our home; she’s so fun to be around. Recently, I introduced her to a reality TV show from 2004, “My Big, Fat, Obnoxious Fiancé,” and her post-anesthesia chat with the nurse had me laughing. 😂 Alyssa called to express her love for me and Kesley, asking me to relay the message. It’s always entertaining to witness the candid moments as the anesthesia wears off. Enjoy the video! Love you Alyssa ❤️

Add 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon vanilla and 1/2 teaspoon of salt, then slowly add 1 1/4 cups of flour once mixed well, add 1/2 cup coconut flakes, 2.5 cups of chocolate chips. We used butter scotch and milk chocolate and it taste so good. Lastly add 3 cups of oats. The dough is the best part. 🤤 Freeze some for later. Bake at 350° for 10-12 minutes. You’re welcome. ❤️

tuEqMiV13dA.description:
The best chocolate chip cookie recipe
Prep:20 mins
Cook: 10 mins

1 cup butter, softened
1 cup white sugar
1 cup packed brown sugar
2 eggs
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
1 teaspoon baking soda
2 teaspoons hot water
½ teaspoon salt
3 cups all-purpose flour
2 cups semisweet chocolate chips but we prefer milk chocolate. Way better 
  
Directions 
Step 1
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Step 2
Cream together the butter, white sugar, and brown sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla. Dissolve baking soda in hot water. Add to batter along with salt. Stir in flour, chocolate chips,  Drop by large spoonfuls onto ungreased pans.

Step 3
Bake for about 10 minutes in the preheated oven. 

Nutrition Facts
Per Serving: 298 calories; protein 3.6g; carbohydrates 38.9g; fat 15.6g; cholesterol 35.8mg; sodium 165.8mg. Full Nutrition

-TsLFcTKlck.description:
Christmas breakfast casserole
In pot melt on stove 
16 ounces cream cheese 
4 tablespoons butter
2/4 cup milk

In a bowl
Beat 12 eggs
2 cups Southern style potatoes
2/4 cup chopped green onion
1 teaspoon salt 
2/4 teaspoon basil
Mix it all together

Combined heated mixture to eggs mixture. Poor into a 9 x 13 pan. And refrigerate overnight.

Cook on 350 for 25 minutes or until cooked in the middle. 
Then Layer shredded zucchini, chopped tomatoes and chopped cream cheese on top.
Then put it back in the oven for another 10 minutes.

Perfect for the young or old, @CanidaePetFood has simplified our eating process. The All Life Stages dog food is a favorite in our house. #AD I love that they use wholesome grains and no corn, wheat, or soy. For my dogs less is best! And since it’s made for dogs of all ages, breeds, and sizes, it really makes mealtime easy in our house. #canidaecrew Available online at PetSmart here: https://www.petsmart.com/dog/food/dry-food/canidae-all-life-stages-dog-food---natural-chicken-5288662.html?lsft=utm_source%3Agoogle%2Cutm_term%3A5288662%2Cutm_medium%3APLA%2Cutm_content%3AGSC%20-%20Medium%20-%20Consumables%20-%20Vendor%20-%20Canidae%20%7C%20Canidae%20-%20Dog%20-%20Food%20-%20Dry%20Food%2Cutm_campaign%3AGSC%20-%20Medium%20-%20Consumables%20-%20Vendor%20-%20Canidae&utm_id=500%7Cpg1050532771%7C775674825045&utm_source=google&utm_medium=PLA&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIyqSphaq26QIVA-iGCh3phwJfEAQYASABEgL9b_D_BwE

PUPPY SCHEDULE 

Feed your puppy 3 times a day. The schedule below is for 3 times. Eliminate the noon meal when she/he reaches 6 months old. 

General guidelines: 
Feed the puppy wait 15 minutes, offer water, and then take him/her out to go potty, then spend 30 minutes to play with puppy.  Puppy soils about every 1 1/2 hrs. Always give water before taking pup out to soil.

6:00 am  

1. Take puppy outside to go to the bathroom
2. Take him to the same spot every morning
3. Initially, take him/her out on leash so she/he has to go in the right spot in the yard 
4. Praise him/her and pet him/her after they potty “good potty!!!”

7:00 am  

1. Feed & water pup
2. Offer them 1/3 of food in morning 
3. Make them sit then put food down and leave it out for 10-15 minutes (even if it’s not gone after 15 min.. put food away. They’ll catch on)
4. Walk pup and take to potty spot
5. Play briefly with puppy
6. Pup stays in crat

Mid morning
1. Walk pup to potty spot
2. Puppy stays with you 15-30 min
3. Pup returns to crate

12-1pm       
1. Feed pup second meal and offer water
2. Walk pup to potty spot
3. Go back inside and stay with pup
4. Pup returns to crate for at least an hour

Mid afternoon:  
1. Offer water
2. Walk pup to potty spot
3. Pup returns to crate

6:00 pm        
1. Feed pup third meal and offer water for the last time (5 hours before bed should be their last time drinking water)
2. Walk pup to potty spot
3. Allow pup to play in kitchen while making dinner, play with kids etc. 

7:00 pm   
1. Walk puppy briefly to potty spot
2. Play with pup until they’re worn out
3. Pup returns to crate

Right before bed   
1. Walk puppy to potty spot
2. Puppy sleeps in crate
